A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Entropic Mirror Monte Carlo, with matching authors, algorithm, and theoretical framework. The main text and complete appendices provide sufficient readable equations, tables, figures, and experimental details for comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendices B–C report original sampling experiments on Gaussian mixtures, Dual Moons, and Two Rings, including quantitative results and proposal-evolution plots.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional results for a 200-dimensional Gaussian mixture and a 550-parameter Bayesian neural-network posterior, including comparisons against MALA and DiGS.

M1.justification: The entropic mixture mapping and Algorithm 1 retain the same sampling, delayed weighting, resampling, and parametric projection procedure. The optional local move already appeared in v1 Appendix D.3. New kernel and Gaussian-mixture configurations instantiate existing components on additional benchmarks.

E1.justification: v2 adds a four-mode mixture embedded in 200 dimensions with irrelevant Gaussian coordinates, a distinct scenario from the retained tensorized mixtures. Section 4.3 also adds synthetic Bayesian regression through a 550-parameter neural-network posterior, substantially extending evaluation beyond the previous mixture and two-dimensional geometry benchmarks.

E2.justification: DiGS is added to the existing RW, NUTS, and AIS comparisons on Dual Moons and Two Rings in Figure 5 and Table 2. The new BNN comparison evaluates MALA and DiGS against EM2C. MALA was previously mentioned as an available kernel, but was not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: For the existing two-dimensional benchmarks, NUTS maximum tree depth changes from 3 to 9; AIS changes from 40 temperatures and 1,000 transitions per temperature to 10 and 100, with proposal scale 2.0 instead of 1.0/0.9. RW is now described as N independent chains rather than one chain. Appendix E.5 introduces explicit evaluation-budget rules and extra iterations for lambda=1. New experiments introduce further configurations and held-out NLL evaluation. These are reported protocol changes, without independently establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.5 adds a focused robustness test isolating ambient dimensionality from the number of modes: four modes in 200 dimensions, assessed through a Wasserstein trajectory and final mode coverage. Existing mixing-parameter, exploration-kernel, and proposal-evolution analyses are largely retained; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: The existing three-run mean ± standard deviation reporting remains. v2 additionally specifies ten runs for the BNN comparison and averages NLL over the final 20 iterations to reduce variability. This does not establish an increase in repetitions for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds DiGS scores, the 200-dimensional results, and BNN NLL results: EM2C 0.1294 ± 0.0707, DiGS 0.2016 ± 0.0128, and MALA 0.2219 ± 0.0170. Existing AIS and NUTS results change; for example, Two Rings AIS SW2 changes from 0.65 ± 0.18 to 0.22 ± 0.18 under revised settings. Several appendix lambda=1 entries are revised or omitted. Main Table 1 and the existing two-dimensional EM2C scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 now explicitly requires 0 < gamma <= (2 C_LS L^2)^(-1), a restriction previously stated only in the supporting Proposition 3. v2 also corrects the GM25 mixture coefficient from 0.2 to 1/25. The central convergence results and appendix proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged, with the intermediate result moved before the theorem proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: combining entropic contraction with Markov exploration, controlling ULA bias, and constructing a practical importance-sampling approximation. The discussion preserves these central claims; the additional experiments provide broader supporting evidence without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly notes that bounded density ratios do not prevent finite-sample weight degeneracy, explains how an unsuitable projection family can collapse modes, and identifies practical lambda tuning as unresolved because admissible values depend on intractable expectations. It also adds interpretations of robustness to irrelevant dimensions and of BNN run-to-run variability.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link and substantial implementation information for DiGS, the high-dimensional mixture, and the BNN experiment, including projection configurations, transition schedules, and evaluation procedures. Appendix E.5 supplies explicit cost formulas and identifies excluded costs. The original flow architecture, tensorized-mixture fitting details, and optional local move are retained rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: Additional citations cover adaptive importance sampling and mirror descent, including Akyildiz and Míguez, Thin et al., and Bianchi et al.; baseline references include Chen et al. for DiGS, Hoffman and Gelman for NUTS, and Neal for AIS. Roberts and Tweedie is added for ULA. These expand attribution and comparison context without substantially changing the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable. v2 makes targeted explanatory rewrites, consolidates experimental details in Appendices B and C, reverses the order of two proof subsections, and moves the former implementation appendix from D to E while inserting BNN details. These are limited organizational and language changes alongside the new scientific material.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one to two columns, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures. Gaussian-mixture tables are consolidated, resolving overlapping subtable content in v1 Table 4. Figure 5 and Table 2 gain DiGS columns; v2 adds the high-dimensional Figure 11, BNN Table 3, and budget Table 7. Several unchanged appendix figures are compressed onto shared pages.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical support beyond v1's tensorized mixtures and two-dimensional targets through a 550-parameter posterior-inference comparison and a stronger DiGS baseline. The corrected theorem assumption, explicit practical limitations, code pointer, and expanded implementation details also improve precision and reproducibility. Budget matching remains approximate and excludes projection costs, so the revision strengthens the evidence without establishing equal-runtime superiority.
